stool-arms-in-out.alt: Two side views of the same student seated on a stool that turns freely on a vertical axle with very little friction. Left: arms stretched out holding a weight in each hand; the student has a large rotational inertia and turns slowly, shown by a thin rotation arrow around the axis. Right: arms pulled in close to the body; the rotational inertia is smaller and the student turns faster, shown by a thicker arrow. The net external torque about the axle is close to zero, so the angular momentum L = Iω stays the same while I falls and ω rises.
